subcategory: feedback adaptation of deployed RAG (correction lag, post-feedback performance) + inference-time feedback memory
task: Open-domain QA under user/expert corrective feedback
problem: RAG systems are evaluated statically although deployed systems are corrected by feedback; existing protocols do not measure how fast and how well corrections propagate to related queries.
architecture: Defines two evaluation axes (correction lag = wall-clock time until updated behaviour; post-feedback performance on semantically related queries). PatchRAG stores feedback in a non-parametric memory and retrieves it with dual intent-context retrieval at inference time, conditioning generation on stored feedback without retraining.
retriever: bge-m3 dense retriever (shared space for user intents and evidence contexts)
knowledge_source: Wikipedia corpus of each dataset plus a feedback memory (~150K synthetic instances for TriviaQA)
key_results: After feedback at step t, PatchRAG averages 62.3 over NQ/TriviaQA/HotpotQA vs 57.3 for RAFT and 56.1 for Golden-only.
NQ EM after feedback 49.8 (PatchRAG) vs 41.9 (RAFT); without feedback, Standard RAG averages 42.1 and Self-RAG 34.7.
Training-based updates show a trade-off between correction lag and post-feedback F1, which the inference-time method avoids.
strengths: Introduces a deployment-relevant evaluation dimension (how quickly corrections take effect) missing from accuracy-only RAG evaluation.
All systems share the same generator and retriever for a fair comparison.

limitations.text: Evaluated in a controlled setting; real-world feedback can be heterogeneous, noisy or interactive.
Accumulated, unresolved or conflicting feedback may require consolidation mechanisms that are not addressed.
Stored feedback may contain sensitive information, raising privacy concerns.

notes: Feedback memory is populated with synthetic instances.
title: Feedback Adaptation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
